title: PV Sindhu's Bengaluru Home Pairs Modern Design With a Mahabharata Chessboard
excerpt: A pastel, three-storey bungalow toured in Farah Khan's vlog mixes turquoise sofas and marble with a Rs 1.7 lakh epic-inspired chessboard, a Persian carpet and a photo wall spanning Sindhu's career and wedding.
body:
• PV Sindhu's new three-storey Bengaluru bungalow, toured in filmmaker Farah Khan's YouTube vlog, pairs pastel, modern interiors with Indian cultural references throughout.
  • The centrepiece is a custom glass-and-marble chessboard inspired by the Mahabharata, with Pandava and Kaurava figures as pieces — reported at around Rs 1.7 lakh.
  • An entrance wall mixes Sindhu's career-defining sporting photographs with wedding pictures of her and husband Venkata Datta Sai; the home also has a Persian carpet, pool and garden seating.
  • Sindhu and her husband reportedly moved to Bengaluru for her high-intensity training camps; the house contrasts with her Hyderabad home in Film Nagar, known for its trophy room and home theatre.

PV Sindhu's Bengaluru home is a study in two registers at once: clean, modern rooms on one side, and unmistakably Indian references on the other. The double Olympic medallist and Padma Bhushan awardee opened the three-storey bungalow to filmmaker Farah Khan for a tour in Khan's latest YouTube vlog, and the details reported by The Times of India and Indulge Express show a house built around both her sporting life and her life after marriage.

The Mahabharata chessboard

The living room sets the tone — a pastel palette, turquoise-blue sofas, a glass centre table and marble accents. Its most talked-about object is a custom chessboard in glass and marble inspired by the Mahabharata. The pieces are detailed figures of the Pandavas and the Kauravas, so every game replays the epic's central confrontation on a board. One report puts the board's price at around Rs 1.7 lakh. A Persian carpet is also among the home's traditional pieces.

The design idea is consistent: the modern shell stays light and uncluttered, while the objects carrying meaning — the epic chessboard, the carpet — carry the cultural weight.

"One report puts the board's price at around Rs 1.7 lakh."

A house that opens with her story

Guests are greeted by a wall of photographs that places career-defining sporting moments alongside snapshots from Sindhu's wedding to Venkata Datta Sai. It is the home's thesis statement at the door: professional milestones and personal ones, given equal space.

The rest of the bungalow follows the same practical pattern. A sunlit dining area opens onto a swimming pool and garden, with seating beside the pool for time outdoors away from training. There is a modular kitchen, and the layout gives the couple room to unwind between camps and tournaments. Sindhu and her husband reportedly moved to Bengaluru so she could focus on high-intensity training camps, and the house reads as a base built for that rhythm — rest and recovery at home, work at the academy.

Bengaluru versus Hyderabad

The contrast with Sindhu's Hyderabad residence is instructive for anyone collecting celebrity-home design ideas. The Film Nagar home is known for its trophy room, home theatre and terrace garden — a house organised around achievement and display. The Bengaluru bungalow keeps the polish but shifts the emphasis: more cultural character, more of the couple's shared life, and photography that mixes the podium with the wedding album.

For diaspora readers furnishing homes abroad, that is the transferable lesson of the tour. The modern-meets-traditional effect here does not come from themed rooms. It comes from a neutral, contemporary base — pastel walls, marble, glass — plus a small number of high-meaning pieces chosen deliberately: one epic-inspired chessboard, one Persian carpet, one wall that tells the family's story. Restraint does the modern part; the objects do the traditional part.
